original_question: For the two 2006 reliability models with state variables Q0(x,t) through Q4(x,t) and P0(x,t) through P6(x,t), representing systems attended by a repairman with vacations and involving boundary conditions such as Q0(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of alpha(x) Q0(x,t) dx + integral from 0 to infinity of mu(x) Q3(x,t) dx + delta(t) and P0(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of alpha(x) P0(x,t) dx + integral from 0 to infinity of mu(x) P3(x,t) dx + delta(t), where lambda is the working rate, mu(x) is the repair rate, and alpha(x) is the vacation rate of the repairman, determine whether these two PDE models are well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of their time-dependent solutions when alpha(x) and mu(x) are non-constant functions.
target_in_paper: The draft does not match the paper’s main problem. arXiv:2405.11510 is centered on the Li–Cao 1994 stochastic scheduling model for an unreliable machine with general up-times and general set-up times, i.e. a two-state elapsed-time PDE system for p0(x,t) and p1(x,t), together with its time-dependent solution, asymptotic behavior in the constant-rate case, and Laplace-transform/evolution-family treatment in the general-rate case.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the paper’s broad analytic themes: a first-order PDE reliability model with elapsed-time variables, Dirac-delta boundary/initial data, and questions about well-posedness and long-time behavior of time-dependent solutions under nonconstant hazard-rate functions.
missing_details: The paper’s actual model is not the pair of 2006 repairman-vacation systems with state families Q0,...,Q4 and P0,...,P6; its advertised model is a two-state stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with state densities p0(x,t) and p1(x,t).

The application setting is stochastic scheduling on an unreliable single machine with general up-times and general set-up/processing times, not a repairman-with-vacations standby/parallel reliability model.

The paper’s state variables have specific meanings: p0(x,t)dx is the probability that at time t the machine is processing job i and the elapsed processing time lies in [x,x+dx); p1(x,t)dx is the probability that at time t the machine is broken down and under repair and the elapsed repair time lies in [x,x+dx).

The relevant hazard-rate functions in the target model are lambda(x), mu(x), and eta(x), corresponding respectively to the random up-time of job i, the random processing time of job i, and the random repair time; alpha(x) as a vacation-rate function belongs to a different model family.

The paper-faithful PDE system needs to be stated explicitly: partial_t p0 + partial_x p0 = -(lambda(x)+mu(x))p0 and partial_t p1 + partial_x p1 = -eta(x)p1, with boundary conditions p0(0,t)=delta(t)+integral_0^infty eta(x)p1(x,t)dx and p1(0,t)=integral_0^infty lambda(x)p0(x,t)dx, and initial data p0(x,0)=delta(x), p1(x,0)=0.

The scope must distinguish the constant-rate case from the general nonconstant-rate case. According to the paper abstract, explicit time-dependent solutions and asymptotic behavior are obtained only in the constant-rate case.

In the general nonconstant-rate case, the paper advertises determination of the Laplace transform of the time-dependent solution and reformulation as an abstract Cauchy problem whose underlying operator is an evolution family; your draft instead asks directly for full well-posedness plus asymptotic behavior of a different model.

A paper-faithful formulation should mention the paper’s methodological point that C0-semigroup theory is said not to be suitable for this model, which is part of the motivation for the evolution-family reformulation.
The elapsed-time domain and quantifiers should be made explicit: x in [0,infinity), t in [0,infinity), with given hazard-rate functions lambda, mu, eta on [0,infinity).
Your draft omits the exact boundary/initial Dirac-delta structure of the target model, which is central to the paper’s framing in the abstract and earlier formulation of the open problem.
refined_question:
Consider the Li–Cao stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with elapsed-time variable x>=0 and time t>=0, governed by
partial_t p0(x,t)+partial_x p0(x,t)=-(lambda(x)+mu(x))p0(x,t),
partial_t p1(x,t)+partial_x p1(x,t)=-eta(x)p1(x,t),
with boundary conditions
p0(0,t)=delta(t)+integral_0^infty eta(x)p1(x,t)dx,
p1(0,t)=integral_0^infty lambda(x)p0(x,t)dx,
and initial data
p0(x,0)=delta(x), p1(x,0)=0,
where p0(x,t)dx is the probability that at time t the machine is processing job i with elapsed processing time in [x,x+dx), p1(x,t)dx is the probability that at time t the machine is under repair with elapsed repair time in [x,x+dx), and lambda(x), mu(x), eta(x) are the hazard-rate functions of the random up-time of job i, the random processing time of job i, and the random repair time, respectively. Determine the time-dependent solution and its asymptotic behavior in the special constant-rate case lambda(x)≡lambda, mu(x)≡mu, eta(x)≡eta, and, in the general nonconstant-rate case, determine the Laplace transform of the time-dependent solution and reformulate the system as an abstract Cauchy problem governed by an evolution family.
equivalent_formulation: In the general nonconstant-rate case, equivalently characterize the model by deriving the Laplace transform of its time-dependent solution and recasting the PDE system with Dirac-delta boundary/initial data as an abstract Cauchy problem whose underlying operator is an evolution family rather than a C0-semigroup.
justification: The paper abstract identifies only one concrete model: stochastic scheduling on an unreliable machine with general up-times and general set-up times, and it describes exactly the constant-rate explicit/asymptotic analysis plus the general-rate Laplace-transform/evolution-family reformulation. This matches the opening unreliability-machine problem in Gupur’s earlier ‘Further Research Problems’ chapter. By contrast, your draft imports a different family of repairman-vacation PDE models from 2006 with state vectors Q0,...,Q4 and P0,...,P6, so it is not paper-faithful. The closest sharp stand-alone question therefore has to be rewritten around the two-state Li–Cao model, while preserving your correct emphasis on time-dependent solutions, well-posedness-type analysis, and asymptotic behavior.
